clusters.state_of_play: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican-born Houston construction business owner who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer during a Tuesday morning enforcement operation as he drove his crew to a job site. ICE claims he attempted to ram his car into officers; eyewitnesses and detainees in the vehicle contradict this, saying he made no threat and was shot through the passenger window. The Department of Homeland Security has acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was originally targeting. Surveillance footage obtained by the New York Times shows ICE agents driving aggressively in unmarked vehicles in the lead-up to the shooting, though the moment of the fatal shot remains unclear. His sons held a candlelight vigil and called for accountability. Houston leaders and a U.S. congressman have condemned the shooting, and calls are growing for a formal investigation amid broader scrutiny of ICE enforcement tactics. Separately, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak — already the fastest-growing ever recorded in Africa, with approximately 1,800 confirmed cases and 600+ deaths — has now spread internationally, with a German hospital treating an infected patient from Congo.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. Families have drawn comparisons to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in central Texas from the prior year. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing dozens and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported.

clusters.state_of_play: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican-born Houston construction business owner who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer during a Tuesday morning enforcement operation as he drove his crew to a job site. ICE claims he attempted to ram his car into officers; eyewitnesses and detainees in the vehicle contradict this, saying he made no threat and was shot through the passenger window. The Department of Homeland Security has acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was originally targeting. Surveillance footage obtained by the New York Times shows ICE agents driving aggressively in unmarked vehicles in the lead-up to the shooting, though the moment of the fatal shot remains unclear. His sons held a candlelight vigil and called for accountability. Houston leaders and a U.S. congressman have condemned the shooting, and calls are growing for a formal investigation amid broader scrutiny of ICE enforcement tactics. Separately, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak — already the fastest-growing ever recorded in Africa, with approximately 1,800 confirmed cases and 600+ deaths — has now spread internationally, with a German hospital treating an infected patient from Congo.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. Families have drawn comparisons to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in central Texas from the prior year. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing dozens and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported.

clusters.state_of_play: Body of 18-year-old Nolan Xavier Wells, a wide receiver at Southwest Mississippi Community College, found Monday off Horn Island, Mississippi, where he was last seen with three white friends over the July Fourth weekend. His mother Christine Wells-Wonsley pleaded publicly for anyone with information to come forward, saying the family just wants to know what happened. His parents say they do not believe he would have stayed behind on the island voluntarily. Attorney Ben Crump and the family have called for an independent investigation, and an independent autopsy is being planned. Rev. Al Sharpton joined the family at a news conference. Tyler Perry has paid for Wells' funeral and made a public plea to the family. Crump has previously said peer pressure led to a significant argument on the boat and that messages were deleted from Wells' cellphone. Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter has previously commented on the case. The family cites many inconsistencies and is seeking answers.

clusters.state_of_play: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican-born Houston construction business owner who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer during a Tuesday morning enforcement operation as he drove his crew to a job site. ICE claims he attempted to ram his car into officers; eyewitnesses and detainees in the vehicle contradict this, saying he made no threat and was shot through the passenger window. The Department of Homeland Security has acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was originally targeting. Surveillance footage obtained by the New York Times shows ICE agents driving aggressively in unmarked vehicles in the lead-up to the shooting, though the moment of the fatal shot remains unclear. His sons held a candlelight vigil and called for accountability. Houston leaders and a U.S. congressman have condemned the shooting, and calls are growing for a formal investigation amid broader scrutiny of ICE enforcement tactics. Separately, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak — already the fastest-growing ever recorded in Africa, with approximately 1,800 confirmed cases and 600+ deaths — has now spread internationally, with a German hospital treating an infected patient from Congo.

Meta faces a fine of up to 6% of global turnover. Additionally, Meta is appealing a landmark Los Angeles jury verdict that found it liable for social media addiction among young users.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with at least five of the dead confirmed as Britons. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. A major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned across the UK this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes. Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.'

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with at least five of the dead confirmed as Britons. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. A major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned across the UK this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes. Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.'

items.title: Floods devastate Bangladesh as dozens killed

ledger.what_new: Floods in Bangladesh killed dozens, left millions stranded with food supply shortages in south-east.
ledger.unique: Entirely separate geography and event — Bangladesh monsoon flooding, not Missouri or China.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. Families have drawn comparisons to the deadly Camp Mystic flooding in central Texas from the prior year. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing dozens and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported.

clusters.state_of_play: An AP-NORC poll reveals strong divisions among US Jews and the broader American public over Israel and Gaza, with Democrats growing notably less supportive of Israel. The same poll finds many Jewish Americans have experienced assault or harassment and feel less safe since Oct. 7, 2023, and that most Jewish adults feel abandoned by and unrepresented by both political parties. A separate poll finds Jewish Americans rate NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani more favorably than Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu; former Republican mayoral candidate Curtis Sliwa said 'it's time for Bibi to go' in response. Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender, warned in a Tel Aviv speech that Israel has become a 'territorial pariah' and that unconditional US support must end, and in a subsequent PBS NewsHour interview called for a new approach to military aid, renewed efforts toward Palestinian statehood, and directly criticized Netanyahu's government. Separately, President Trump amplified a 49-minute expletive-laden video by far-right pundit Michael Savage on Truth Social, titled 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISM MUST BE CRIMINALIZED; LEADERS DEPORTED,' in which Savage attacks Mamdani and calls for the deportation of Democratic Socialists.

clusters.state_of_play: A global heat wave event is unfolding: South Korea recorded 39.9°C in the southeast on July 11, a day after elevating heat alerts nationwide, and on July 12 issued its first-ever 'grave' heat wave warnings for Gyeongsan and Pohang; the suffocating heat wave is expected to persist through at least Monday July 14. Europe is experiencing its third wave of extreme heat this summer, with at least 12 killed in a Spanish wildfire; Germany faces another scorching week though no records are expected; the UK has extended an Amber heat health alert as parts enter a second week of temperatures above the heatwave threshold, with 'exceptional' wildfire risk flagged, two swimmers found dead, and the Met Office warning the heatwave will last until at least next week with a thunderstorm risk developing in the south. Over 40 million people in England face hosepipe bans or restrictions, and 2026 has become the first year on record to see UK temperatures of 35C or higher in three calendar months. In the United States, a heat dome has peaked across the western U.S., placing 40 million people under heat alerts, with triple-digit highs expected in the Southwest and Great Plains, and many cities now forecast to see record overnight temperatures this week.

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with at least five of the dead confirmed as Britons. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. A major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned across the UK this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes. Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.'

clusters.state_of_play: The death toll from the major wildfire in southern Spain's Andalusia/Almería region stands at 13, with at least five of the dead confirmed as Britons. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez visited the wildfire site in Almería, met firefighters and emergency crews, and called for Spain to strengthen prevention measures. Victims' families have alleged they received no evacuation order from authorities. The missing count has been revised down to 10 as the fire stabilised, allowing hundreds of evacuees to return to their homes; the blaze has burned around 7,000 hectares (~25 sq miles). British survivor Malcolm Timbrell, 70, from the village of Bédar, told of surviving in his car while his wife Annette Kilgore and friends died trying to run to safety. A British man died while on the phone to his wife after returning to rescue cats, and two British hikers were found alive but badly burned in a ravine. A 93-year-old British woman admitted Friday with 20% burns to Torrecardenas University Hospital died Sunday night. Separately, a wildfire of 'exceptional scale' is burning near Paris amid France's third heat wave since May, adding to Europe's worsening fire crisis. A major incident remains declared in Wales where at least 10 wildfires burned across the UK this weekend, including a blaze near Conwy Mountain prompting evacuation of 36 homes. Climatologist Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele warned 'We are not prepared enough for the conditions that fuel these fires.'

ledger.what_new: A German hospital is now treating a Congo Ebola patient, indicating international spread.
ledger.unique: First evidence of outbreak crossing into Europe via patient transfer to Germany.

clusters.state_of_play: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, a Mexican-born Houston construction business owner who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer during a Tuesday morning enforcement operation as he drove his crew to a job site. ICE claims he attempted to ram his car into officers; eyewitnesses and detainees in the vehicle contradict this, saying he made no threat and was shot through the passenger window. The Department of Homeland Security has acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was originally targeting. Surveillance footage obtained by the New York Times shows ICE agents driving aggressively in unmarked vehicles in the lead-up to the shooting, though the moment of the fatal shot remains unclear. His sons held a candlelight vigil and called for accountability. Houston leaders and a U.S. congressman have condemned the shooting, and calls are growing for a formal investigation amid broader scrutiny of ICE enforcement tactics. Separately, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak — already the fastest-growing ever recorded in Africa, with approximately 1,800 confirmed cases and 600+ deaths — has now spread internationally, with a German hospital treating an infected patient from Congo.
